Bootstrap confidence band for an ensemble fit

Source: R/ensemble.R
ensemble_bootstrap_ci.Rd

Two resampling schemes are supported. method = "poisson" implements the parametric bootstrap of the manuscript's simulation study: bootstrap pseudo-observations are drawn as \(y_k^{(b)} \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(f_{ens}(t_k))\), appropriate when the data-generating process is itself (approximately) Poisson, as in the simulated growth curves used there. method = "residual" instead resamples the standardised fitted residuals with replacement and adds them back onto the fitted curve, which is appropriate for real surveillance counts: the Poisson scheme assumes \(\mathrm{Var}(y_k)=f_{ens}(t_k)\), which is routinely violated by over-dispersed daily death/case counts (reporting batches, weekday effects), producing artificially narrow bands (see the real-data application in the manuscript, where this is checked directly). In both cases the full ensemble (all three growth models, re-weighted) is refit to each replicate, and percentile confidence limits are taken across the B replicates at every requested time point.

Usage

ensemble_bootstrap_ci(
  fit,
  newdata = NULL,
  method = c("poisson", "residual"),
  B = 500L,
  level = 0.95,
  beta_fixed = 1.5
)

Arguments

fit

An ensemble_fit object.

newdata

Numeric vector of times at which to build the band (defaults to fit$t; include out-of-window times for a forecast band).

method

"poisson" (default) or "residual".

B

Number of bootstrap replicates.

level

Confidence level.

beta_fixed

Passed to fit_ensemble() for each replicate.

Value

A list with boot_curves (B x length(newdata) matrix) and ci (data frame with time, lower, upper, fit).
